title: Evaluate the inner value
text: First, calculate the inner value: what is $$\cos\left(-\frac{\pi}{6}\right)?$$

subHints.title: Connection to the unit circle
subHints.text: Recall that $$\cos\left(\frac{-\pi}{6}\right)$$ represents the $$x-$$ coordinate of the point on the unit circle at the angle $$\frac{-\pi}{6}.$$

subHints.title: Find equivalent angle geometrically
subHints.text: The principal range of $$\arccos$$ is $$[0, \pi], $$ which covers only the 1st and 2nd quadrants. Angles in the 4th quadrant share the same $$x-$$ coordinate as angles directly above them in the 1st quadrant. Visually, a vertical line drawn up from the point on the circle at angle $$\frac{-\pi}{6}$$ intersects the upper half of the circle at the point on the circle at angle $$\frac{\pi}{6}.$$\n##figure1.gif##

subHints.title: Find equivalent angle algebraically
subHints.text: We can also verify this algebraically. Because cosine is an even function, $$\cos\left(\frac{-\pi}{6}\right)=\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{6}\right).$$ Since $$\frac{\pi}{6}$$ falls inside the required principal range of $$[0, \pi], $$ that is our final answer.
